rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic lexica offer competing senses for ʿaṣr: time or period, a time of day, morning, late afternoon or evening; the dual can mean day and night.
rows.anchor: Die arabischen Lexika verzeichnen eine Reihe von z. T. gegensätzlichen Bedeutungen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since other opening oaths name specific daytimes or night phases, ʿaṣr probably denotes a particular time rather than time in general.
rows.anchor: stellt wohl auch ʿaṣr eine spezifische Zeitangabe dar und bezeichnet nicht allgemein „Zeitspanne“

rows.speaker: Cuypers
rows.claim: Cuypers reads ʿaṣr as a general span of time, though the commentator notes that he gives no further justification.
rows.anchor: „Zeitspanne“ o. Ä. (so ohne weitere Begründung Cuypers 1999, 47)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If ʿaṣr means late afternoon, this oath differs from all other early Meccan oaths naming night or stages of morning and forenoon.
rows.anchor: Falls wirklich der Spätnachmittag intendiert ist, so hebt sich Q 103 von allen anderen frühmekkanischen Schwüren

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic oaths likely draw on a characteristic pre-Islamic seer expression, a relationship that has not yet been adequately studied.
rows.anchor: wahrscheinlichen, aber bis dato noch nicht hinreichend untersuchten Anlehnung an ein charakteristisches Ausdrucksmittel altarabischer Seher

rows.speaker: Spitaler
rows.claim: Medina II joins the oath verse to verse 2 in its verse division.
rows.anchor: Medina II zieht V. 1 zu V. 2 (Spitaler, Verszählung, 72)

rows.speaker: Neuwirth
rows.claim: Neuwirth treats the oath as an independent verse, in keeping with other sura-opening oaths.
rows.anchor: Wie die anderen Schwüre am Surenanfang ist aber auch wa-l-ʿaṣr als eigenständiger Vers zu sehen (Neuwirth, Studien, 35)

rows.speaker: Zirker
rows.claim: The German translation of the verse follows Zirker.
rows.anchor: Die Übersetzung folgt Zirker.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse may mean that human conduct causes people to forfeit bliss in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: Gemeint ist vielleicht, dass der Mensch aufgrund seines Verhaltens der jenseitigen Seligkeit verlustig geht

rows.speaker: Torrey
rows.claim: Torrey compares this eschatological loss with Luke 9:24; the Syriac Peshitta uses ḥsar, from the same root as Arabic ḫasira and ḫusr.
rows.anchor: Von einem eschatologischen „Verlust“ ist, wie Torrey 1892, 32, anmerkt, auch in Lukas 9:24

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Philippians 3:7–8 offers another comparison for the notion of loss.
rows.anchor: Vgl. a. Paulus Brief an die Philipper 3:7.8

rows.speaker: Torrey
rows.claim: Torrey documents many other Qur'anic examples of ḫasira and ḫusr used eschatologically.
rows.anchor: Für einen eschatologischen Gebrauch von ḫasira, ḫusr im Koran gibt es noch zahlreiche weitere Belege

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An early Meccan parallel is the phrase ḫāsirah in Q 79:12.
rows.anchor: In frühmekkanischer Zeit vgl. noch 79:12 (qālū tilka ʾiḏan karratun ḫāsirah)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three-rhyme sura is an opening single-member oath by late afternoon, followed by a rebuke; verse 3 exempts believers and differentiates good from bad people.
rows.anchor: Die auf 3Kr reimende Sure besteht aus einem eingliedrigen Schwur „beim späten Nachmittag“ mit rügendem ʾinsān-Spruch als Schwuraussage

rows.speaker: Neuwirth
rows.claim: Neuwirth argues that oaths by prayer times preserve the recipient's liturgical experience and give the sura a hymn-like tone.
rows.anchor: Neuwirth schreibt Schwüren bei Tages- und Nachtzeiten allgemein die Funktion zu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentator finds no hymn-like resonance in this sura and points to a critical discussion of Neuwirth's hypothesis elsewhere.
rows.anchor: Eine solche hymnische Konnotation klingt jedoch im vorliegenden Text nirgends nach

rows.speaker: Robinson
rows.claim: Robinson's secular reading makes ʿaṣr the time when merchants count a day's earnings, linking the oath's image of profit to the eschatological loss in verse 2.
rows.anchor: Robinsons profane Deutung des ʿaṣr als des Zeitpunkts, zu dem Händler am Ende eines Markttags ihre Einnahmen berechnen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Robinson's reading is strengthened by Q 104, which also contrasts worldly wealth with damnation in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: Robinsons Interpretation überzeugt auch angesichts des sich ergebenden Bezugs zu Q 104

rows.speaker: Neuwirth
rows.claim: A prayer-time meaning for afternoon nevertheless remains possible.
rows.anchor: dass mit dem Nachmittag doch eine Gebetszeit gemeint sein könnte (so Neuwirth, Frühmekkanische Suren, 157)

rows.speaker: Rudolph
rows.claim: Rudolph compares the sura's polemic against ostentatious prayer with Matthew 6:5, where hypocrites pray publicly to be seen by people.
rows.anchor: Gegen eine äußerliche Verrichtung des Gebets polemisiert schon Matthäus 6:5

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Q 68:12 and 70:21 provide parallels for withholding good or help.
rows.anchor: Vgl. 68:12 (mannāʿin li-l-ḫairi muʿtadin ʾaṯīm) und 70:21 (wa-ʾiḏā massahu l-ḫairu manūʿā)

rows.speaker: Geiger
rows.claim: Geiger derives māʿūn from Hebrew māʿôn, meaning dwelling or refuge, and interprets the verse as denying shelter to people seeking help.
rows.anchor: Geiger leitet den Ausdruck māʿūn von hebr. māʿôn, „Wohnung“ und auch „Zuflucht“, her

rows.speaker: Nöldeke
rows.claim: Nöldeke accepts Geiger's derivation but rejects the assumption that Arabic must preserve the Hebrew word's original meaning.
rows.anchor: Nöldeke (1910, 28) akzeptiert Geigers Ableitung, lehnt jedoch die Annahme ab

rows.speaker: Nöldeke
rows.claim: Nöldeke cites al-Aʿshā Maimūn's verse praising someone as more generous with his benefits than a foaming Euphrates channel, supporting the sense benefit or gift.
rows.anchor: einen Vers von al-Aʿšā Maimūn, in dem es über den Gelobten heißt

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hebrew loan māʿūn apparently already meant benefit, gift, or donation in pre-Qur'anic Arabic.
rows.anchor: Der ursprünglich aus dem Hebräischen stammende Ausdruck māʿūn hatte also offenbar bereits in vorkoranischer Zeit die Bedeutung „Wohltat“, „Spende“ o. Ä. angenommen

rows.speaker: Rhodokanakis
rows.claim: Rhodokanakis agrees with Nöldeke and explains the Arabic semantic development through interference from maʿūna, from root ʿ-w-n.
rows.anchor: Rhodokanakis angeschlossen, der die eigenständige Bedeutungsentwicklung von arab. māʿūn durch Interferenz mit arab. maʿūna

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A deliberate Qur'anic echo of Hebrew māʿôn remains possible despite the Arabic word's changed meaning.
rows.anchor: Gleichwohl ist nicht auszuschließen, daß die koranische Verwendung des Ausdrucks bewußt den Anklang an hebräisch māʿôn sucht

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second section opens with the emphatic wail that introduces a catalogue of vices.
rows.anchor: einen rhetorisch markanten Einsatzpunkt auf, nämlich die einen Lasterkatalog einleitende Interjektion „Wehe …“ (wail)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 4–6 target the criticized people's neglect of ritual prayer.
rows.anchor: Die anschließenden Verse zielen zunächst (V. 4–6) auf die kultische Nachlässigkeit der Getadelten ab

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing verse adds refusal of assistance, generalizing the earlier failure to support orphans and the poor, who represent socially vulnerable people in the Hebrew Bible.
rows.anchor: Die am Ende der ersten Versgruppe exemplarisch angeführte Unterlassung der Unterstützung besonders schwacher Gesellschaftsmitglieder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two groups cross-correspond: verse 1 and verses 4–6 concern religious omissions, while verses 2–3 and verse 7 concern social omissions; the first group stresses social failings and the second religious ones.
rows.anchor: Inhaltlich korrespondieren insofern V. 1 und V. 4–6 (religiöse Unterlassungen) und V. 2.3 und V. 7 (soziale Unterlassungen)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Māʿūn and manaʿa are near-anagrams built from permutations of the same consonants, m-n-ʿ and m-ʿ-n.
rows.anchor: die zwei unterschiedliche Permutationen desselben Konsonantenbestandes (m-n-ʿ / m-ʿ-n) enthalten

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rare hapax māʿūn was likely chosen instead of a commoner word for its assonance with manaʿa; the sound pattern sharpens the contrast between expected assistance and its denial, a figure later rhetoricians call reversed paronomasia.
rows.anchor: in der Terminologie späterer Rhetoriker handelt es sich um die Stilfigur des ǧinās maqlūb

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening oath may refer to the familiar fig and olive trees.
rows.anchor: والتين والزيتون قد يكون قصد بهما الشجران المعروفان

rows.speaker: مفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes explain the paired trees as two kinds, one whose fruit has no seed and one whose fruit has a seed.
rows.anchor: ذكر المفسرون لاختيار هذين الشجرين للقسم بهام أسبابا عدة، فقد ذكروا أنه أقسم بنوعين من الشجر

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet received a plate of figs, ate them, and told his companions that if any fruit came from Paradise, it would be this one because Paradise's fruit has no seeds.
rows.anchor: أنه أُهديَ لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم طبق من تين فأكل منه وقال لأصحابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Adam used fig leaves to cover his nakedness after it was exposed in Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر أن آدم خصف من ورقه ليستر عورته حين انكشفت في الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an describes the olive tree as blessed.
rows.anchor: وأما الزيتون فإنه شجرة مباركة كما جاء في التنزيل العزيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author speculates that the eight verses might correspond to Paradise's eight gates, but leans toward this being pure conjecture.
rows.anchor: فإن عدد آيات هذه السورة ثمانية وهُنَّ بعددِ أبواب الجنة. قد يكون هذا القول خَرْصاً محِضاً وأنا أميلُ إلى ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He notes numerical patterns elsewhere: eight repetitions of the blessing question in descriptions of Paradise and seven in warnings, corresponding to Paradise's and Hell's gates.
rows.anchor: عند الكلام في وصف الجنة ثماني مرات بعدد أبواب الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other proposed numerical patterns say Sura al-Qadr has thirty words for Ramadan's days and places huwa at word 27 to signal the 27th night.
rows.anchor: وقالوا: إن سورة القدر ثلاثون كلمة بعدد أيام شهر رمضان، وإن قوله: (هي) في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cautions that many such numerical correspondences may simply be coincidences.
rows.anchor: وعلى أي حال فإن كثيراً من هذه العلاقات ربما كانت موافقات والله أعلم

rows.speaker: مفسرون
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes fig and olive as two Holy Land mountains, called Tour Tina and Tour Zaita in Syriac, where those trees grow.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن المقصود بالتين والزيتون جبلان من الأرض المقدسة يقال لهما بالسريانية طور تينا وطور زيتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the mountain interpretation, the connection between the two names and what follows is not clear without strained reasoning.
rows.anchor: والعلاقة بين التبين والزيتون وما بعدهما ليس ظاهرة على هذا إلا بتكلُّف

rows.speaker: مفسرون
rows.claim: A reported interpretation identifies three places of major prophetic missions: Jerusalem for Jesus, Sinai for Moses, and Mecca for Muhammad.
rows.anchor: هذه محال ثلاثة بعث الله في كل واحد منها نبياً مرسلاً من أولي العزم أصحاب الشرائع الكبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tibyān reads the oath as the three prophetic places and explains them as successive manifestations of Jesus, Moses, and Muhammad and their major religious communities.
rows.anchor: جاء في (التبيان في أقسام القرآن)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tibyān says the oath ascends from the place of Jesus to Moses and then Muhammad, paralleling a Torah passage about Sinai, Seir, and Paran.
rows.anchor: ونظير هذا بعينه من التوراة التي أنزلها الله على كليمه موسى: (جاء من طور سيناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the three prophetic locations because their relation to one another is clear on that reading.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو الراجح فيما أرى لأن المناسبة بين هذه المحالّ المُقْسَمِ بها ظاهرة على هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence begins with fig then olive, with olive ranked higher because God calls it blessed; it serves as fruit, food, and lamp oil.
rows.anchor: والزيتون أشرف وأفضل من التين فقد شهد الله له أنه شجرة مباركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sinai is superior to the preceding places because God spoke with Moses there and sent him to Pharaoh and his people.
rows.anchor: فإنه الجبل الذي كَلَّم الربُّ عليه موسى وناجاه وأرسله إلى فرعون وقومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites al-Wahidi's statement that exegetes agree the tree from Mount Sinai in Q 23:20 is the olive.
rows.anchor: والمفسرون كلهم يقولون إن المراد بهذه الشجرة شجرة الزيتون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mecca is the best and most beloved place to God, the Prophet's birthplace and mission site, and home of the Kaaba, guidance for all peoples.
rows.anchor: وهو أفضل البقاع عند الله وأحبها إليه كما جاء في الحديث الشريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath progresses from fig to olive to Sinai to the secure city, moving from the noble to the noblest and ending at the home of the final, most honored mission.
rows.anchor: فأنت ترى أنه تدرّج من التين إلى الزيتون إلى طور سينين إلى بلد الله الأمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The epithet al-amīn is deliberately chosen because it can mean both trustworthy and secure, and both senses are intended.
rows.anchor: فالأمين وصف يحتمل أن يكون من الأمانة، كما يحتمل أن يكون من الأمن. وكلا المعنيين مراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a place of trust, Mecca receives the trust of revelation through Gabriel, the trustworthy spirit, to Muhammad, the truthful and trustworthy recipient.
rows.anchor: فالرسالة أمانة نزل بها الروح الأمين وهو جبريل، وأداها إلى الصادق الأمين وهو محمد، في البلد الأمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rūḥ al-Maʿānī explains the city's trustworthiness as protecting whoever enters it, like a trustee guarding what is entrusted to him.
rows.anchor: وأمانته أن يحفظ مَنْ دخله كما يحفظ الأمين ما يُؤتَمَنُ عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a place of security, Mecca was safe before and after it became a city, as Abraham prayed for its safety and God answered.
rows.anchor: فهو البلد الآمن قبل الإسلام وبعده، دعا له سيدنا إبراهيم عليه السلام بالأمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites Qur'anic assurances that whoever enters is safe and that the House was made a sanctuary for people.
rows.anchor: وقد استجاب الله سبحانه هذه الدعوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-amīn can be an intensive active adjective meaning safe, or a passive form meaning protected from harm.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون (الأمين) فعيلاً بمعنى مفعول، مثل: جريح بمعنى مجروح وأسير بمعنى مأسور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rūḥ al-Maʿānī gives both active and passive analyses: safe or trusted, with the people inside protected from harm.
rows.anchor: الأمين فعيل بمعنى فاعل أي الآمن من أمُن الرجل بضم الميم أمانةً فهو أمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ likewise allows al-amīn to mean safely inhabited or protected, including birds and animals, or a place entrusted with its inhabitants' safety.
rows.anchor: وأمين للمبالغة أي: آمنٌ مَنْ فيه ومن دخله وما فيه من طير وحيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The choice of al-amīn rather than the more usual āmin combines security and trust, active and passive senses, and literal and figurative meanings.
rows.anchor: أنه باختياره لفظ (الأمين) جمع معنيي الأمن والأمانة، وجمع معنى اسم الفاعل واسم المفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath's answer fits the preceding places of revelation: it describes humanity's beginning in the best form and its eventual return to the lowest state.
rows.anchor: فإنه أقسم بالراسالات على بداية الإنسان ونهايته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People divide into those who accept the prophetic call and those who refuse it; most are returned low, while believers receive reward.
rows.anchor: ثم لما كان الناس في إجابة هذه الدعوة فريقين منهم مَنْ أجاب ومنهم من أبى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because revelations provide a way of life for humans, the answer names human nature in verse 4 and the way of life in verse 6; a proper way must suit human nature.
rows.anchor: فذكر طبيعة الإنسان في قوله: {لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الإنسان في أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ} وذكر المنهج في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is explicitly the subject of creation because this verse celebrates divine power and artistry; Qur'anic descriptions of bounty similarly assign the action to God.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنه في موطن بيانِ عظيمِ قدرتهِ وحسن فعله وبديع صنعه فأسند ذلك إلى نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By contrast, passive creation forms are used when the point is human weakness or defects.
rows.anchor: في حين قال: {وَخُلِقَ الإنسان ضَعِيفاً} [النساء: 28]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming God as creator also shows that humanity's guide and lawgiver is its creator, who best knows what benefits people; a passive form would not state this clearly.
rows.anchor: فأراد أن يبين أن واضع المنهج للإنسان هو خالق الإنسان ولا أحد غيره أعلم بما يَصلحُ له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is also named as the one who returns people low to emphasize divine control over both the beginning and end of human life.
rows.anchor: أراد أن يذكر أن بيده البداية والنهاية، وأنه القادر أولاً وأخيراً لا معقب لحكمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had the verse said people were returned low in the passive, it could suggest another agent undoes God's creation.
rows.anchor: لكان يفهم ذاك أن هناك ردّاً غيره يفسدُ خلقته ويهدم ما بناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Best form covers the human being's appearance, meaning, perception, and every material or immaterial excellence.
rows.anchor: على أحسن ما يكون في الصورة والمعنى والإدراك وفي كل ما هو أحسن من الأمور المادية والمعنوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma marks temporal delay before the low state and a great difference in rank between the best form and the lowest state.
rows.anchor: فهي من حيث الوقت تفيد التراخي، كما أنها من حيث الرتبة تفيد التراخي

rows.speaker: مفسرون
rows.claim: One interpretation takes asfal sāfilīn as extreme old age, with physical and mental decline until the person knows nothing.
rows.anchor: الهرم وضَعْف القُوى الظاهرة والباطنة وذهول العقل حتى يصير لا يعلم شيئاً

rows.speaker: مفسرون
rows.claim: On the old-age interpretation, righteous elderly people continue receiving the reward they earned when healthy and strong.
rows.anchor: إن الصالحين من الهرمى لهم ثواب دائم غير منقطع يُكْتَبُ لهم في وقت شيخوختهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says that when a believer is returned to extreme old age, his deeds are recorded as they were during his strength.
rows.anchor: إنَّ المؤمن إذا رُدّ لأرذل العمر كُتِبَ له ما كان يعمل في قوته

rows.speaker: مفسرون
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes asfal sāfilīn as the lowest places, Hell or its lowest level; the exception then straightforwardly excludes the righteous.
rows.anchor: وذهب آخرون إلى أن المقصود به أسفل الأماكن السافلة وهو جهنم أو الدرك الأسفل من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fī Ẓilāl al-Qurʾān focuses on spiritual capacities: rejecting faith reverses humanity's potential to rise above angels, making it fall below animals that follow their nature.
rows.anchor: والتركيز في هذا المقام على خصائصه الروحية. فهي التي تنتكس إلى أسفل سافلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this reading, believers preserve and complete their natural capacities through faith and good works, reaching their intended perfection.
rows.anchor: فهؤلاء الذين يبقون على سوء الفطرة ويكملونها بالإيمان والعمل الصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse can encompass all these interpretations of the lowest state.
rows.anchor: وظاهر أن معنى الآية يتسع لكل ما ذكروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nonbeliever's life is also low, distressed, and unhappy, as shown by Qur'anic descriptions of a constricted life and a fall into a remote place.
rows.anchor: وهي تفيد أيضاً أن حياة غير المؤمن نكد وغم، وعيشة ضنك وشقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception here requires faith and good works, whereas al-ʿAṣr adds mutual exhortation to truth and patience; that added practice prevents further loss of reward.
rows.anchor: فلم يقل مثل ما قال في سورة العصر: {والعصر * إِنَّ الإنسان لَفِى خُسْرٍ * إِلاَّ الذين آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ الصالحات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tibyān says al-ʿAṣr narrows its exception because loss includes foregone reward from failing to exhort others, while this sura's exception is broader because exhortation is additional to personal faith and good works.
rows.anchor: فمن لم يكن كذلك فقد خسر هذا الربح فصار في خسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tibyān distinguishes duties one performs personally from the additional duty or merit of enjoining right and forbidding wrong, which can be individual, communal, or recommended.
rows.anchor: فإن الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر مرتبة زائدة. وقد تكون فرضاً على الأعيان. وقد تكون فرضاً على الكفاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exhortation covers obligatory and recommended truth and patience; those who do it gain extra reward, while those who only meet personal duties lose that extra gain without being utterly ruined.
rows.anchor: وإن كان أولئك لم يكونوا من الذين خسروا أنفسهم وأهليهم. فمطلق الخسارة شيء والخسار المطلق شيء

rows.speaker: مفسرون
rows.claim: Ghayr mamnūn is explained either as undiminished or uninterrupted reward, or as reward unspoiled by reproachful reminders.
rows.anchor: قيل: ومعنى غير ممنون غير منقوص ولا منقطع، وقيل: معناه غير مكدر بالمنّ عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author takes all senses of ghayr mamnūn as intended, describing reward that is lasting and free from reproach.
rows.anchor: والحق أن كل ذلك مراد وهو من صفات الثواب، لأنه يجب أن يكون غير منطقع ولا مُنَغَّصاً بالمِنَّة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added fa in fa-lahum gives the reward sentence a connection suited to this sura's context, unlike the parallel wording without fa in al-Inshiqāq.
rows.anchor: ثم انظر كيف زاد الفداء في قوله: {فَلَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ} ولم يفعل مثل في آية شبيهة بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Inshiqāq spends many verses on disbelievers and their punishment but says little about believers, so omitting fa suits its concise reward statement.
rows.anchor: فانظر كيف أطال في وصف الكافرين وأعمالهم وعقابهم، وأوجز في الكلام على المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Inshiqāq begins with human toil and successive ordeals, whereas al-Tīn begins by honoring humanity; its fa therefore suits the emphasis on continuing, unclouded reward.
rows.anchor: في حين بدأ في سورة الين بتكريم الإنسان فقال: {لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الإنسان في أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ} فناسب ذلك تأكيد استمرار أجره وعدم تنغيصه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the evidence just given, nothing should make a person deny the final judgment.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: أي شيء يجعلك أيها الإنسان مكذّباً بالجزاء بعد هذه الدليل الواضح؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human development from a drop into a balanced person, through successive stages, proves the creator can resurrect people after death; failure to create them again would be no more difficult than creating them first.
rows.anchor: فإن الذي خلقك أقدر على أن يعيدك بعد موتك وينشئك خلقاً جديداً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The judgment argument is tightly connected to the preceding account of human creation and decline.
rows.anchor: فانظر جلالة ارتباط هذا الكلام بما قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura combines transmitted evidence for judgment, through the revelations given to Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad, with rational evidence from human creation and development.
rows.anchor: فالدليل النقلي هو ما أخبرت به الرسالات السماوية، وقد ذكر من هذه الرسالات كبراها وهي رسالات موسى وعيسى ومحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word dīn is chosen instead of recompense, reckoning, or resurrection because it fits the preceding revelations and can mean both religion and judgment; the creator gives humanity the best way to live.
rows.anchor: وذلك لما تقدم ذكر مواطن الرسالات ناسب ذلك ذكر الدين، لأن هذه أديان، ولأنه قد يراد بذلك معنى (الدين) علاوة على معنى الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥkam al-ḥākimīn can mean the greatest in wisdom and governance or the supreme judge, since ḥukm can refer to wisdom or adjudication.
rows.anchor: و (أحكم الحاكمين) يحتمل أن يكون معناه أعظم ذوي الحكمة وأحسنهم تدبيراً، ويحتمل أن يكون معناه، أقضى القاضين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If it means greatest in wisdom, God's perfect wisdom entails resurrection and recompense; otherwise the good and evil would go unanswered, which would contradict divine wisdom.
rows.anchor: تعَيَّنت الإعادة والجزاء لأن حكمته تأبى أن يُتركَ الإنسان سدى ولا يحاسب على أعماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If it means supreme judge, God will decide disputes among people, as in Q 39:46.
rows.anchor: فيحكم بين عباده فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون، كما قال تعالى: {أَنتَ تَحْكُمُ بَيْنَ عِبَادِكَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase compresses four related meanings: wisest ruler, wisest judge, most discerning adjudicator, and best governor.
rows.anchor: إذ كل لفظ من (أحكم الحاكمين) يحتمل أن يكون بمعنى القضاء والحكمة فيكون قد جمع أربعة معان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concluding question is deliberative rather than declarative, inviting the listener to affirm the judgment personally, as in Q 21:56.
rows.anchor: ثم انظر كيف جعل ذلك بأسلوب الاستفهام التقريري ولم يجعله بالأسلوب الخبري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending returns to the opening: the one who sent the great revelations and their exalted laws is the wisest judge.
rows.anchor: فإن الذي أنزل هذه الشرائع العظيمة وما تضمنته من أحكام سامية هو أحكم الحاكمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse endings were chosen to carry several meanings at once: al-amīn joins safety and trust, asfal sāfilīn old age and Hell, ghayr mamnūn lasting and unreproached reward, dīn religion and recompense, and aḥkam al-ḥākimīn wisdom and judgment.
rows.anchor: ثم انظر إلى التنسيق الجميل في اختيار خواتم الآي
